scope.flow: Permissionless initialization of UUPS proxy contracts (DistributionCreator, Distributor) allowing governance takeover
scope.environment: UUPS proxy deployment of DistributionCreator and Distributor contracts

statements.text: Every freshly deployed proxy starts with the initialized flag at zero.
The initialize function in DistributionCreator (and Distributor) uses only the initializer modifier and has no access control on the caller.
Both contracts are set up behind UUPS proxies where the constructor with initializer runs only on the implementation, not on each proxy instance.
The first external address calls initialize on the freshly deployed proxy.
The attacker initializes the proxy to point accessControlManager to a malicious contract that always treats them as governor or guardian.
initialize lacks caller access control, so the first external caller sets accessControlManager (and distributor address and default fees in DistributionCreator) without authorization.
Initialization of a proxy should only be performed by an authorized party, not by the first arbitrary external caller.
The accessControlManager set during initialization should not be an attacker-controlled contract that treats the attacker as governor or guardian.
onlyGovernor, onlyGovernorOrGuardian, and onlyUpgradeableInstance checks should not be under attacker control after initialization.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker must be the very first caller or merely any caller before legitimate initialization.
Report does not specify the exact timing/order relative to legitimate deployment or initialization by the protocol team.
Report does not state whether initialize can be called more than once or whether the initializer modifier prevents re-initialization after takeover.
